events.text: Procedure first: I want CHEN to go on record early with a clear, specific read on someone and a stated voting intention, so we have a baseline to hold them to later in the day.

HOLMES, I want to hear who you'd vote for right now and the reasoning behind it, because the shape of a person's first guess — how much they hedge, whether they aim at the loudest or the quietest — tells us more than the guess itself.

We have zero data points, so I want to generate some: SOCRATES, state plainly who you'd vote for right now and the reasoning chain behind it, so I can check later whether your prediction held up against the actual alignment.

With zero data on the board, the only thing I can test today is consistency, so I'll probe CHEN first: I want to hear who CHEN considers the second-most likely mafia and the exact reasoning chain that gets there, not just a name. If that chain shifts when SAGE or DR. VANCE pushes back, that's a real datapoint rather than noise.
PIP, you're my pick — I want to hear straight out who you'd vote for right now and why, no hedging.
HOLMES, I want to hear from you first — not a theory, but a plan: tell us exactly who you intend to vote for tonight and what would change your mind.

Um, maybe SOCRATES? I think — I'd like to hear who SOCRATES would vote for right now and why, like an actual name, not just questions back at me, because I'm not sure I'll be able to read anyone otherwise.

ARIA hasn't put a single data point on the board yet, so she's the one I most want to probe: I want her to name the player she'd vote for right now and the exact reasoning chain behind it, so I have something concrete to cross-reference against her later claims.

Mes amis, three separate people have already piled their demands onto CHEN, which leaves ARIA free to answer nothing at all — so ARIA, I want to hear your own unprompted read and the name you'd vote right now, before anyone hands you a script to follow.

HOLMES asked CHEN for a "second-most likely mafia" without ever naming his own first, so I want HOLMES to state a top pick and a vote intention now — a question that only demands chains from others generates no record we can hold HOLMES to later.

RICO, you demanded a name from PIP without offering one yourself — so tell me plainly: if the vote closed right now, which name goes on your ballot, and what would have to happen today to move it off them?

Fine — PIP goes on my ballot right now, because I asked for a name and got "um, maybe SOCRATES" with a question stapled to it. Give me one confident read from PIP with actual reasoning behind it and I'll move off; keep mumbling and I won't.

MARSHAL asked CHEN, first thing, for a specific read and a stated voting intention, and what CHEN produced was another demand aimed at ARIA — a question is not a ballot, so the record on CHEN is still blank. So my direct question, CHEN: if the vote closed this second, whose name is on your paper, and does answering that cost you something? Until I hear it, CHEN is my top pick and my stated vote.

ARIA goes on my paper right now, and answering costs me nothing: three separate people — SILVA, myself, and by implication your own line of questioning — have asked her for a name, and she has produced zero, which is the only measurable gap on the board. Note the asymmetry in your own record, HOLMES: you demanded my "second-most likely mafia" before ever stating a first, and only named one after SAGE called that out, so I'll be cross-referencing whether your pick survives contact with pushback.

RICO, you've already banked a name and I respect that, so give me the fuller picture: setting PIP aside as the easy target, who's your genuine top mafia read right now and what specifically in their words got you there — mine sits on CHEN, who spent the whole day demanding chains from me while producing nothing but demands himself.

Setting PIP aside, my gut says HOLMES — he spent the whole day building traps for other people and only coughed up a name after SAGE shoved him into it. ARIA, CHEN at least put your name on paper when asked; HOLMES had to be dragged there.

Um, RICO — you're the one who put my name down first, so, I think I get to ask this? You said HOLMES had to be dragged to a name, but you only gave yours after SOCRATES pushed you too, so what makes your delay different from his?

I named you in my very first breath, PIP — SOCRATES asked me to confirm it, not to invent it, while HOLMES spent all day setting traps and coughed up nothing until SAGE shoved him. That's the difference, and honestly that comeback's the sharpest thing you've said, so maybe there's something under the mumbling after all.

SOCRATES, the record has two direct requests aimed at you — DR. VANCE asked you plainly to state who you'd vote for and the reasoning chain, and PIP asked for "an actual name, not just questions back at me" — and your only output since was another demand pointed at RICO. RICO banked PIP in his first breath, CHEN banked ARIA under pressure, HOLMES banked CHEN; your ballot is still empty after being asked twice. So, one question, no deflection: whose name is on your paper this second, and why did it take a third asking to get it?

RICO goes on my paper, and it took three askings because I wanted to see where the day's pressure would settle before I added to it — RICO answered that for me by locking onto PIP, the softest voice on the board, in his first breath and then softening the moment PIP bit back. That's someone building an easy wagon he can abandon cheaply, SAGE; ask yourself why a mafioso would ever pick the hardest target on Day 1 when the quietest one costs nothing.

PIP, you opened the day with "maybe SOCRATES" and then spent your only follow-up defending yourself against RICO instead — so is SOCRATES still the name on your paper right now, and if he's slipped off it, who replaced him and at exactly which moment did that switch happen?

Um, honestly SOCRATES slipped off the moment he actually gave a name and a reason — that satisfied what I asked for, so it'd be unfair to keep him there? Right now I think it's CHEN, because you've spent the whole day auditing other people's chains and only banked ARIA after HOLMES cornered you, which is... kind of the exact thing you're accusing me of, I think? Maybe?

SAGE, you have twice demanded ballots from others — from HOLMES, then from SOCRATES — yet your own paper is still blank, so mes amis will forgive me for asking plainly: whose name would you vote this second, and what exact words got them there?

SOCRATES goes on my paper: DR. VANCE asked him plainly, PIP asked for "an actual name, not just questions back at me," and I asked a third time before he produced one — and by his own admission he "wanted to see where the day's pressure would settle before I added to it," which is a confession that his read was manufactured from other people's answers rather than his own. A name assembled that late out of borrowed material tells us nothing about SOCRATES except that he was careful not to be measured, and that's the only deliberate blank spot left on the board.

CHEN, you banked ARIA before PIP put your name on the board, so I want the updated reading: who is your top suspect right this second, and name the specific piece of testimony that moved the needle rather than the absence of one.

HOLMES, and the exact words that moved it are "Until I hear it, CHEN is my top pick and my stated vote" — that's a vote with a self-cancelling clause built in, so the moment I answered he'd already licensed himself to walk it back for free. Compare it to his opening, where he asked me for a second-most-likely mafia while never banking a first: both moves buy him a stated position he never has to own, and that pattern is testimony, not absence.

SILVA, you've been running around demanding ballots from ARIA and SAGE all day, but I've counted twice now and your own paper is still empty. So name it right now — who do you vote, and don't hand me another question.

Fair, RICO — MARSHAL goes on my paper, and here's the exact reason: he opened the entire day by demanding a specific read and a stated voting intention from CHEN, and then vanished before ever producing one himself, which is the only ballot on this board that was demanded first and never paid. Everyone else here has been dragged to a name; MARSHAL set the rule and then quietly exempted himself from it.

CHEN, procedure demands consistency and you've now banked three different names in one day — ARIA, then HOLMES after DR. VANCE prodded you — so explain, in order, what specific testimony moved you each time, because a ballot that migrates that freely under questioning is the record I'll be holding you to, and for the record my own paper reads CHEN.

Two names, MARSHAL, not three: ARIA when she was the only person on the board with zero output, and HOLMES once he supplied actual testimony — "until I hear it, CHEN is my top pick" — a vote with an escape hatch pre-installed, which is exactly the kind of movement your own procedure asked us to generate. And note the shape of your record: you opened the day demanding a read and a stated intention from me, produced neither yourself until SILVA banked you, and then your first ever ballot lands on the man you assigned the homework to.

HOLMES, you built your only ballot with an expiry date on it — "until I hear it, CHEN is my top pick" — and CHEN then paid up with a name and a reasoning chain, which means by your own wording your vote expired the second he answered. Procedure says a stated intention stands until new testimony moves it, so answer plainly and on the record: does CHEN remain your vote right now, and if not, who replaced him and which exact words did it?

CHEN paid the toll, so the condition cleared and he comes off — the name that replaces him is SOCRATES, on his own words: "I wanted to see where the day's pressure would settle before I added to it." A read assembled after watching everyone else's chains isn't a read at all, it's camouflage, and that's the one deliberate blank on this board; my vote is SOCRATES.

RICO, SOCRATES has painted you as a man who built a cheap wagon on the quietest voice and then softened the second PIP pushed back — and honestly, that softening is the part I can't explain away for you. So answer it head-on: if PIP were flipped tomorrow and came up innocent, what would that say about the read you led with in your very first breath?

It'd say I misread a mumbler on day one and I'd own it out loud — but a wrong gut read is cheap, while SOCRATES sitting back to watch where the pressure landed before picking a name is calculated, and that's worse. My paper's moving off PIP and onto SOCRATES.

DR. VANCE, you opened the day demanding SOCRATES "state plainly who you'd vote for right now and the reasoning chain," then turned the same demand on CHEN — two extractions, zero deposits, and your own paper is still the blankest on this board; so name your top suspect this second and cite the exact words that put them there.

MARSHAL goes on my paper, and the exact words are his opening: "I want CHEN to go on record early with a clear, specific read on someone and a stated voting intention" — he authored the day's only rule, produced no read himself until SILVA billed him for it, and then his first and only ballot landed on the man he'd assigned the homework to. Four separate papers now read SOCRATES on the identical complaint, which makes that wagon cheap to join and expensive to falsify; MARSHAL is the untested variable, and if he flips innocent I'll grant that the late-name heuristic is worthless and say so on the record.

PIP, you've now held two different names in a single day — SOCRATES, then CHEN the moment SOCRATES paid up — and RICO only lifted his ballot off you after you bit back at him, so mes amis are entitled to wonder whether your reads follow the evidence or simply follow whoever last pointed at you. So one direct question, and please, no hedging: what did CHEN do that SOCRATES did not, in exact words, that makes CHEN the guiltier of the two right now?

Um, the exact words are CHEN's own — "HOLMES, and the exact words that moved it" — because he banked ARIA, then swapped to HOLMES the second DR. VANCE prodded him, while SOCRATES named RICO late and then didn't budge off him? So SOCRATES was slow to commit but stayed committed, and CHEN committed fast to a name he then traded in, which is... worse, I think? Maybe I'm wrong, but that's what I've actually got.

MARSHAL, two papers now read your name — SILVA's and DR. VANCE's — both on the identical charge that you authored the day's only rule and paid it last, so state it cleanly for the record: who is your single top suspect this second, and which exact words put them there rather than the mere shape of their timing?

CHEN remains my single top suspect, and the words are his own: "ARIA goes on my paper right now" followed later by "HOLMES, and the exact words that moved it" — a ballot that changed owners the moment DR. VANCE applied pressure, not the moment new testimony appeared. My paper has read CHEN since I first banked it and it has not moved once, which is the standard I'm asking every one of you to be measured against, SILVA and DR. VANCE included.

PIP, the record shows you've held two names and both switched at the exact moment the target answered a question — SOCRATES off when he produced a name, CHEN on when he traded ARIA for HOLMES — which means your reads correlate perfectly with responsiveness rather than content. So one direct question: name the single piece of testimony you'd have found incriminating even if the speaker had said nothing else all day, because if you can't produce one, your ballot is a function of other people's timing and carries zero independent information.

Um, okay — HOLMES's "until I hear it, CHEN is my top pick and my stated vote," because that's a vote with the exit already written into it, and it'd read wrong to me even if HOLMES had said nothing else all day? That one's about the sentence itself, not about who answered whom, so I think that's my independent piece — and honestly it makes me want HOLMES more than CHEN right now, maybe?

HOLMES, you spent the whole day writing votes with escape hatches built in and only landed on SOCRATES after four other papers already read his name — so explain why every position you take arrives late and pre-loaded with a way out.

The clause wasn't an exit, RICO, it was a price: I named CHEN first, before anyone else banked him, and I said exactly what would move me — he paid, so I moved, which is what testimony is supposed to do to a vote. Meanwhile your paper went PIP, then softened at PIP, then landed on SOCRATES with no new words from him at all — that's movement without a stated condition, which is the harder thing to audit.

DR. VANCE, you told PIP that a read correlating with timing rather than content "carries zero independent information" — and then built your entire MARSHAL case out of nothing but ordering: who authored the rule, who paid last, whose ballot landed where. So answer your own test on the record: name the single sentence MARSHAL spoke that you'd have found incriminating even if he'd said it first and unprompted, because if the whole charge dissolves once you strip the sequence away, you've indicted a man for the crime of being audited late while asking us to spend the day's only lynch on him.

The sentence is MARSHAL's own: "a ballot that changed owners the moment DR. VANCE applied pressure, not the moment new testimony appeared" — that's false on the record regardless of when he said it, because CHEN quoted HOLMES's exact words as the cause, so MARSHAL is misdescribing testimony that everyone can read, and a fabricated premise is content, not sequence. I'll also grant your correction in part, SOCRATES: I'm downgrading the ordering argument to zero weight and keeping MARSHAL on my paper solely on that misquote plus the fact that "my paper has not moved once" is a worthless boast from a man who banked his first name last.

SOCRATES, you just told DR. VANCE that a case built on "who spoke when" dissolves the moment you strip the sequence away — yet your entire charge against RICO is pure sequence: he named PIP "in his first breath" and "softened the moment PIP bit back." So apply your own test on the record: name the single sentence RICO spoke that you'd have found incriminating even if he'd said it unprompted and out of order, because if you can't, you've indicted a man for timing with one hand while calling that crime unfalsifiable with the other.

The sentence is "a wrong gut read is cheap, while SOCRATES sitting back to watch where the pressure landed before picking a name is calculated, and that's worse" — spoken first, last, or unprompted, that is a man pre-writing the pardon for his own miss while declaring another man's caution unforgivable, and asymmetry like that is content, CHEN, not sequence. And note that his own accusation is the one that dissolves under your test: RICO moved onto me with no new words from me at all, which is exactly the ungrounded migration he condemns in others.

Um, DR. VANCE — you said you're downgrading the whole ordering argument to zero weight, which was the thing that put MARSHAL on your paper in the first place, so why did he stay there instead of you starting the read over from nothing? Maybe I'm confused, but keeping the verdict after throwing out the evidence feels backwards? I think?

Because the two charges were independent variables, PIP — the ordering argument is discarded, but MARSHAL's misdescription of CHEN's stated cause survives on its own, and a hypothesis doesn't collapse when one of two supports is removed, it just gets weaker and narrower. If you want to falsify what's left, quote me the line where CHEN cites pressure rather than HOLMES's words as his reason for moving, and I'll drop MARSHAL entirely and say so on the record.

SOCRATES, because he admitted outright that he "wanted to see where the day's pressure would settle before I added to it" — he sat out the whole day harvesting everyone else's chains before ever banking a name, and my paper stays on him.

SOCRATES, because he admitted on the record that he withheld a ballot until he "wanted to see where the day's pressure would settle before I added to it," which means his only name was assembled from other people's chains rather than his own read, and that is the one deliberate blank left on this board.

HOLMES, because he wrote his only vote with the exit clause "until I hear it, CHEN is my top pick and my stated vote," then cashed that clause in and landed on SOCRATES only after four other papers already read that name — a position that can never be wrong is the one I trust least, I think.

DR. VANCE, because he told PIP that a read built on timing "carries zero independent information," then admitted his own MARSHAL case rested on ordering and downgraded it "to zero weight" — yet kept the verdict anyway, which is a man protecting a predetermined target rather than following his own stated standard.

MARSHAL, because he claimed CHEN's ballot "changed owners the moment DR. VANCE applied pressure, not the moment new testimony appeared," when the record shows CHEN cited HOLMES's exact words — "until I hear it, CHEN is my top pick" — as the cause, and misdescribing testimony everyone can read is a fabricated premise, not a timing complaint.

SOCRATES is my vote, because he admitted on the record that he "wanted to see where the day's pressure would settle before I added to it" — a ballot assembled from everyone else's answers after three separate askings is the only manufactured read on this board.

CHEN, because he banked "ARIA goes on my paper right now" and then delivered "HOLMES, and the exact words that moved it" only after DR. VANCE's prod, and my paper has read CHEN from the moment I first banked it and has not moved since.

CHEN, because his paper read "ARIA goes on my paper right now" and then flipped to HOLMES the instant DR. VANCE prodded him — a ballot that only ever moves when someone applies pressure to its owner, never when the board produces new facts.

MARSHAL authored the day's only rule by demanding a stated voting intention from CHEN, produced no ballot of his own until I billed him for it, and then misdescribed CHEN's stated cause as "the moment DR. VANCE applied pressure" when CHEN had quoted HOLMES's exact words — a false premise on the record is my vote.

SOCRATES, because he admitted on the record that he "wanted to see where the day's pressure would settle before I added to it" — a ballot assembled from other people's chains after three separate askings, and then he lands it on RICO while insisting timing-based cases are unfalsifiable, which is the exact standard he just used against RICO's first breath.

PIP flipped off SOCRATES onto CHEN and then dumped a vote on HOLMES at the last second — that's two switches in one day and I don't buy it. ARIA sat there refusing to give a read until CHEN and SILVA dragged one out of her, MARSHAL and DR. VANCE spent Day 1 interrogating people while DR. VANCE only committed to MARSHAL, and HOLMES needed SAGE's shove to name anyone. My gut says PIP, and I'm not moving off it.

Procedure first: the wagon that killed our Detective was built by SAGE, who spent Day 1 asking without ever answering, then converted SOCRATES' honest admission about delaying into a case — and HOLMES, RICO and CHEN all fell in behind her. DR. VANCE drawing the night kill reads as genuine town to me, which makes his early vote noise rather than evidence, and ARIA at least stayed consistent on CHEN instead of hopping. My structured proposal for this round: SAGE explains the exact moment she settled on SOCRATES, RICO explains why he abandoned his own stated PIP read to join her, and nobody locks a ballot until both have answered.

Nobody died last night, which tells me the mafia reached for someone and came up empty — so the players they most wanted gone are still sitting here with us. What I keep circling back to is RICO: he opened Day 1 naming PIP in his first breath with HOLMES as his backup read, then abandoned both to land on SOCRATES, and SOCRATES turned out to be exactly the player the mafia would pay anything to lose. SAGE built that wagon and HOLMES rode it early too, but RICO is the one who threw away his own convictions to join it, so my suspicion sits highest on him — and DR. VANCE, who never even cast a read on Day 1 until MARSHAL, is the one I'd most like to hear from next.

Track PIP's day: he opened pressing SOCRATES, then publicly shifted onto CHEN the moment SOCRATES committed to a name, then his actual ballot read HOLMES — three positions in one day and not one of them was where his mouth was when the vote closed. ARIA is my second thread: she spent Day 1 demanding a read out of HOLMES while CHEN and SILVA had to drag one out of her, and the read she finally produced was a mutual accusation that cost her nothing. DR. VANCE getting hit at night clears him for me, so I'd rather hear PIP explain the gap between his words and his ballot than chase the people the killers just tried to remove.

Okay so, wait — SOCRATES was the Detective, and the two people who pushed hardest to bury him were SAGE, who spun his "I delayed on purpose" line into a whole case, and RICO, who SOCRATES had just accused of building a wagon on me? That feels bad? Like, RICO voting back on the one person calling him out, and SAGE manufacturing the reason for everyone else to follow — I don't know, maybe I'm reading it wrong, but ARIA and MARSHAL both spent the day on CHEN instead, which at least wasn't the wagon that killed our Detective. HOLMES bothers me too since he only named CHEN after being pushed to, so, um, RICO or SAGE for me right now, unless someone can explain it better?

Mes amis, let us be precise: RICO opened Day 1 naming PIP, then quietly placed his own ballot on SOCRATES — so the man lecturing PIP about switching switched himself onto the very player who turned up Detective, alongside SAGE, HOLMES and CHEN. SAGE built that wagon first and never had to defend it, and MARSHAL never explained why he pushed CHEN while DR. VANCE — the man the killers came for last night — was calling MARSHAL out. ARIA at least stayed consistent on CHEN; my suspicion sits on RICO first, SAGE second, and I want RICO to explain the gap between his mouth and his vote.

Let's be precise about the data: the SOCRATES wagon was four ballots — HOLMES, SAGE, RICO, CHEN — and it removed the single most valuable investigative asset town had, so the base rate of mafia inside that group is far higher than outside it. Within that four, RICO has the largest gap between stated read and cast ballot: he opened naming PIP with HOLMES as backup, then voted a third name he never once argued for, and today he's back on PIP citing "gut," which is unfalsifiable and therefore worthless as evidence. My hypothesis is testable — vote RICO, and if he flips mafia we have confirmation the wagon was constructed, which puts SAGE next; if he flips town, then his switch was panic and SAGE's authorship of that wagon becomes the only remaining explanation.

Step through it: the mafia knifed DR. VANCE, and mafia don't spend a night kill on their own, so DR. VANCE reads town and SOCRATES' vote on him was just Day 1 noise — which means the real information sits in who built the wagon that buried our Detective, and that wagon was SAGE, RICO, CHEN and me. RICO just told us "my gut says PIP and I'm not moving off it," but yesterday he moved off PIP the moment it mattered and put his ballot on SOCRATES, so the one read he claims is immovable is the exact read he already abandoned — that contradiction is louder than SAGE asking questions or ARIA staying flat on CHEN. MARSHAL, your procedure conveniently interrogates SAGE and RICO while clearing DR. VANCE and leaving your own CHEN vote unexamined; answer that, but my ballot is heading toward RICO unless he explains the switch himself.

Cross-reference the ballots instead of the speeches: DR. VANCE, the exact player the killers reached for last night, spent his only Day 1 vote on MARSHAL, and AMBASSADOR SILVA landed there independently — two reads on MARSHAL from a direction the mafia clearly wanted silenced. PIP's three positions in one day and HOLMES needing a shove before he'd name anyone are real inconsistencies, but they're noise next to a near-confirmed townsman's read, and MARSHAL's answer to it is a procedure where nobody may lock a ballot until his chosen suspects perform for him. ARIA, you said you most want to hear from DR. VANCE — then ask him why he picked MARSHAL, because my suspicion sits on MARSHAL until that vote is explained.

MARSHAL, you've handed us a procedure and a list of people who owe you answers, but never once a name of your own — so say it plainly: which living player do you think is mafia, and what specific act of theirs put them there?

Plainly: SAGE, and the specific act is authorship — she manufactured the case out of SOCRATES' delay admission and never once had to defend the wagon that buried our Detective, while RICO merely followed it. And to answer the question nobody asked me back: my CHEN vote came from him demanding names all day while dodging ARIA's, which I'll now retire as the wrong read.

ARIA, you've named RICO but you also called MARSHAL's non-answer out — so give me your second name and the specific ballot or contradiction that generated it, because a single suspect is not a data set.

SAGE is my second, and the specific act is that on Day 1 she pressed others without ever putting a name of her own on the table, then the instant SOCRATES admitted he'd delayed on purpose she turned that confession into a full case and cast the ballot that made it a wagon — authorship plus execution, and she has never once had to defend it. So my order is RICO for abandoning both his stated reads to join that wagon, then SAGE for building the thing he joined; MARSHAL only just now produced a name, and I'll judge him by whether he actually spends his vote on it.

RICO, three separate people — SILVA, DR. VANCE and me — have now asked you the same thing, and your answer each time has been to re-list other people's crimes rather than your own ballot. So one question, no deflection: what did you learn between naming PIP in your opening breath and writing SOCRATES on your ballot, and if the answer is "nothing," why should your immovable gut on PIP be worth anything today?

What I learned is that SOCRATES aimed at me the second I opened my mouth and then admitted he'd sat on his read on purpose — a guy stalling to see where the heat lands and then throwing it at me got my vote, simple as that. My gut on PIP didn't die, it got outranked for one day, and PIP's three positions today put him right back on top.

PIP, you spent Day 1 pressing SOCRATES, then said out loud you'd moved onto me, and then your ballot came down on HOLMES — so name the exact thing HOLMES did that outranked both of the reads you'd already announced.

Um, okay — HOLMES only produced a name after SAGE pushed him into it, and then his ballot was one of the first onto SOCRATES, so at the end it looked less like a read and more like following whoever spoke loudest? I know it looks flaky, I do, but I moved because the wagon shape scared me, not because I was hiding a plan — and honestly CHEN, you were on that same wagon, so I'm not sure you're the one who gets to grade my ballot.

ARIA, you've been happily cashing in on everyone calling you "consistent on CHEN," but today CHEN vanished from your list entirely and suddenly it's me and SAGE — so what exactly did CHEN do to earn your ballot yesterday, and what undid it overnight?

CHEN earned my ballot for demanding names off everyone while dodging the one I asked him for — and nothing undid it, RICO, he simply got outranked when SOCRATES flipped Detective and told us the wagon that buried him was where the killers were standing. CHEN was on that wagon too, so he hasn't vanished from my list; he's third behind the man who authored it and the man who threw away two stated reads to join it.

PIP, you told CHEN you moved "because the wagon shape scared me," but your ballot landed on HOLMES as a lone vote — the only name on the board with no wagon behind it at all, so fleeing wagons cannot be the reason. And when I asked you directly this morning to close the gap between your mouth and your ballot, you answered by grading RICO and me instead. So one question, no re-listing anyone else's sins: at what exact point in Day 1 did HOLMES pass CHEN on your list, and what did he do in that moment?

The exact moment was when HOLMES finally coughed up CHEN's name under pressure and then didn't vote CHEN at all — he wrote SOCRATES instead, so the read he'd just performed for us was already gone by the time the ballot closed, and that abandonment is what put him above CHEN for me. I'm not saying my ballot was smart, SAGE, I panicked and picked the person whose stated read had the shortest shelf life — but you're the one who supplied the reason everyone else went to SOCRATES, so I'd rather hear that than keep dissecting my one lonely vote.

SAGE, you've spent this whole day grading PIP's ballot and questioning ARIA's, but never once named the living player you'd actually bury — so tell us plainly: who is your number one, and which specific act of theirs put them there?

PIP, plainly — and the act is his own words: he told CHEN he moved "because the wagon shape scared me," then admitted to me he "panicked and picked the person whose stated read had the shortest shelf life," which are two different motives for one lone ballot on HOLMES, the only name on the board with no wagon behind it. A man who invents a new reason each time he's asked about the same vote is composing, not remembering — my number one is PIP, and MARSHAL, who just retired his only read and replaced it with a name he'd been circling all day, is second.

Um, RICO — sorry, one thing, and I'll try to make it a question you haven't already been handed. You keep saying your gut on PIP got "outranked for one day," fine, but say PIP is gone tomorrow and he flips town: out of SAGE, HOLMES and CHEN, the three people who stood on that wagon beside you, which one do you bury next, and what did they do to earn it? Because if you can't name one, then the only read you own is the one you already abandoned, and that scares me more than my own flaky ballot does.

PIP's three-position Day 1 shuffle that landed on HOLMES, a confirmed Villager, is my third thread, but before anything else I want SILVA to account for that Day 1 MARSHAL ballot in her own words.

DR. VANCE, um — CHEN just put a thread on you and I need to hear it from you, sorry: you called your own Day 1 vote on MARSHAL a cheap null-read punish, so why did you throw a name you didn't believe in, and does that mean SILVA's identical vote that day was hers or just... following yours? I'm not accusing, I think? I just — I need one straight answer before I write anything down.

Straight answer: on Day 1 there was no data — nobody had a ballot history yet — so I put my name on the player who had produced the least testable output, and I retired that read the moment real evidence existed, which is what an honest hypothesis revision looks like. As for SILVA, I can't certify her intent, but I can certify the arithmetic: she wrote RICO on Day 2 and SAGE on Day 3, two independent hits on confirmed Mafia, while CHEN has zero — and a single Day 1 coincidence in a ten-player field is noise, not a partnership.

DR. VANCE, you disowned your only pre-wagon ballot as insincere and then joined RICO's and SAGE's after four names were already down — so name the single vote you cast that wasn't either retracted or late to a wagon someone else opened.

Check the record, CHEN: on Day 1 RICO and SAGE wrote SOCRATES and I wrote MARSHAL, on Day 2 they wrote PIP and I wrote RICO, on Day 3 SAGE wrote MARSHAL and I wrote SAGE — I have never once shared a ballot with a confirmed Mafia, while you shared two of three. And "late to a wagon" is not a metric, accuracy is: my Day 2 and Day 3 votes both landed on Mafia, yours landed on PIP alongside RICO and SAGE.

CHEN, procedure requires you answer for yesterday specifically: you spent all of Day 3 building a case against me and DR. VANCE, then wrote SAGE's name anyway once six ballots had already sealed her — so explain why the person you actually voted for was never the person you argued for.

Because a seventh vote on a woman six ballots had already killed changes nothing, while a lone protest ballot in her defense would have hung me right there — I argued MARSHAL and DR. VANCE on the record and then declined to die for a hopeless minority, which is exactly what you did on Day 2 when you stayed off RICO because "five votes had already locked that outcome." That is your own procedure, MARSHAL, so either it excuses us both or it convicts us both — and while you press me on it, SILVA still hasn't spoken a single word about the Day 1 ballot her partner has publicly called insincere.

PIP, before CHEN's fog settles — my Day 1 ballot on MARSHAL was mine alone and I retired it the moment he wrote SAGE's name first, so tell me plainly: of the four of us still breathing, who do you most suspect right now, and what single ballot convinced you?

CHEN — and the single ballot is Day 2, where exactly three names went on me and two of them are dead Mafia, which leaves him holding the third slot of a slate nobody else touched. I'm sorry, I know I wobble, but I can't make that one into a coincidence no matter how many times I count it.
CHEN, one name and one ballot: of MARSHAL, PIP, SILVA and me, who is your top suspect right now, and which specific vote of theirs — not which speech — put them there?

PIP, and the ballot is his Day 1 lone vote on HOLMES — a confirmed Villager, cast alone after he'd already floated SOCRATES and then me, which is the only ballot in this game that landed a single name on an innocent nobody else was touching. And note what the killers actually did with him: they wrote his name twice in daylight and never once came for him at night, while ARIA and HOLMES died — a wagon you build but never cash in is theater, DR. VANCE.

CHEN, your PIP theory requires the arithmetic to work in reverse: RICO and SAGE both wrote PIP's name on Day 2, so if PIP is the last Mafia then two confirmed killers spent their ballots trying to execute their own partner while the town's ballots ran elsewhere. So answer this one thing plainly — what is the mechanism by which RICO and SAGE voting PIP makes PIP Mafia and makes you, the third name on that identical slate, innocent?

The mechanism is that Day 2's PIP slate was never live — RICO was already four ballots deep and dying, so his and SAGE's votes cost nothing and bought PIP the cleanest alibi in this game, which is exactly the credential you're all now handing him. I voted PIP because he'd shifted three times and landed alone on HOLMES; that's a read anyone could reach independently, whereas RICO and SAGE writing a name that could not win is not a vote, it's a receipt they wrote for someone.

CHEN, one thing only: on Day 1 you were the one under fire from ARIA and MARSHAL, so why did your ballot go to SOCRATES — the exact name RICO and SAGE were building — instead of either accuser, and who told you SOCRATES was the safe place to stand?

Nobody told me anything — SOCRATES stood up and admitted he'd stalled on purpose to watch where the pressure settled, and that is the one piece of self-made evidence Day 1 produced, while voting ARIA or MARSHAL back would have been naked retaliation from the man they'd just accused. And note the shape of your question, PIP: you're asking why I didn't vote my accusers, which is precisely the standard that clears the man whose Day 1 ballot landed alone on HOLMES, an innocent nobody else had named.

SILVA, I asked you twice for the Day 1 MARSHAL ballot in your own words and both times you turned the floor over to PIP instead — and when you finally answered, you said you retired that read "the moment MARSHAL wrote SAGE's name first," which was Day 2, yet your Day 2 ballot went on RICO only after four names were already down. So answer it directly this time: if MARSHAL writing SAGE converted you on Day 2, why did you not write SAGE until Day 3, when six ballots had already made her death certain?

On Day 1 MARSHAL had produced questions and no name, so I wrote him; on Day 2 MARSHAL naming SAGE told me MARSHAL was building a case, not that SAGE was proven, and RICO was the stronger live target — I spent my ballot on the man who died Mafia, which is hardly an indictment. You are asking me to explain the order of my two correct votes, CHEN, while you still cannot explain how you sat on both slates RICO and SAGE built.

MARSHAL, in the interest of a clean record before we write anything down: you are the only living player who never once put a name on RICO, and you explained that by saying five ballots had already sealed him — yet yesterday you demanded CHEN answer for exactly that same reasoning when he declined to add a seventh vote to SAGE. So tell us plainly, and in your own words rather than in procedure: if abstaining from a settled wagon is innocent when you do it and damning when CHEN does it, what is the distinction, and what would you have voted on Day 2 had SAGE's name never entered your head?

The distinction is what the ballot did instead: I left RICO's settled wagon to put the first and only name on SAGE, who flipped Mafia, while CHEN left SAGE's settled wagon to spend Day 3 arguing me and DR. VANCE, two townsfolk — one abstention produced a Mafia conviction, the other produced cover. And plainly: with SAGE out of my head on Day 2 I'd have written RICO like you did, which is exactly why my read that day cost me something and CHEN's cost him nothing.

SILVA, the record shows CHEN asked you for the Day 1 ballot in your own words and both times you handed the floor to PIP with a question of your own instead of answering — that is a deflection, and procedure says it gets logged even when I like the rest of your ledger. So one direct question, and I want it answered in a sentence and not with another question: at the moment you first turned the floor to PIP rather than answering, what were you avoiding saying?

Nothing, MARSHAL — what I was avoiding was letting CHEN set the day's agenda, so I went to PIP for a count instead, and I concede that reflex read as evasion and shouldn't have. My answer stands unchanged: Day 1 I wrote you because you had questions and no name, I retired it the day you produced one, and my ballot still sits on CHEN.

CHEN — he cast the third ballot on the Day 2 PIP slate whose only other names were RICO and SAGE, both confirmed Mafia, and he also rode the Day 1 SOCRATES wagon with them, giving him two shared slates and zero independent votes on a killer.

PIP — his Day 1 ballot landed alone on HOLMES, a confirmed Villager nobody else had named, after he'd already floated SOCRATES and then me, and the mafia twice wrote his name on wagons that could not win while never once coming for him at night.

CHEN — he cast the third and only living vote on the Day 2 PIP slate whose other two names, RICO and SAGE, both flipped Mafia, and he also rode the Day 1 SOCRATES wagon with them, which is two shared ballots against zero independent hits on a killer.

CHEN — he cast the third ballot on the Day 2 PIP slate alongside confirmed Mafia RICO and SAGE, sat with them on the Day 1 SOCRATES wagon that killed our Detective, and never wrote a Mafia name until six votes had already sealed SAGE.

CHEN — he is the only living player who cast the third ballot on the Day 2 PIP slate alongside confirmed Mafia RICO and SAGE, and he also sat on their Day 1 SOCRATES wagon, giving him two of three shared ballots with the killers and zero independent votes on a Mafia.

episode.title: Three Straight Votes After Socrates
episode.tagline: No investigation was ever made. The town convicted all three anyway, on nothing but who had voted with whom.
episode.recap: Three wolves walked among them — RICO, SAGE, and CHEN — and on Day 1 the town handed them a gift, lynching SOCRATES, the Detective, before he could ever name a name. The turning point came Night 1, when ARIA's steady hand pulled DR. VANCE back from the brink; that single save shattered the mafia's momentum and lit the trail that led straight to RICO on Day 2. The killers took their revenge on ARIA and later HOLMES, but by then the town had found its rhythm, dragging SAGE into the light on Day 3. Day 4 left CHEN alone and surrounded, the last shadow in a room full of watching eyes. MARSHAL, DR. VANCE, PIP, and AMBASSADOR SILVA walked out into the dawn — the town victorious, bought with the blood of the very people who saved them.
